name: Indonesian Low-Resource NMT Benchmark
description: Neural machine translation (NMT) for low-resource local languages in Indonesia faces significant challenges, including the need for a representative benchmark and limited data availability. This work addresses these challenges by comprehensively analyzing training NMT systems for four low-resource local languages in Indonesia: Javanese, Sundanese, Minangkabau, and Balinese. Our study encompasses various training approaches, paradigms, data sizes, and a preliminary study into using large language models for synthetic low-resource languages parallel data generation. We reveal specific trends and insights into practical strategies for low-resource language translation. Our research demonstrates that despite limited computational resources and textual data, several of our NMT systems achieve competitive performances, rivaling the translation quality of zero-shot gpt-3.5-turbo. These findings significantly advance NMT for low-resource languages, offering valuable guidance for researchers in similar contexts.
evaluation_method: BLEU (commonly reported; chrF also used in some experiments)
typical_sota_score: 10–35 BLEU (varies widely by language and training/augmentation strategy)
reputation: A recent, focused benchmark addressing low-resource Indonesian languages that is gaining attention within low-resource MT and regional NLP research communities.
notes: Small/low-resource corpora; results strongly depend on data augmentation (synthetic parallel data) and preprocessing; possible contamination risk when synthetic data or large web-trained models overlap with evaluation domains.
